solutions.question: What is the meaning of the word entrepreneur and its origin?
steps: An entrepreneur is a person who identifies a business opportunity, takes risks and organises resources to start and run a business.
The word entrepreneur comes from the French word “entreprendre,” which means “to undertake.”
solutions.answer: An entrepreneur undertakes the risks and work of starting a business; the word comes from the French word “entreprendre.”

solutions.question: How do digital technologies help entrepreneurs reach a global audience?
steps: Digital technologies such as websites, social media and online marketplaces allow businesses to promote and sell their products through the internet.
The internet helps entrepreneurs communicate with customers in different countries and reach a global audience.
Online tools can also support customer service, payments and delivery arrangements.
solutions.answer: Digital technologies help entrepreneurs promote and sell products to customers around the world.

solutions.question: What is an e-commerce platform, and why is it important for businesses?
steps: An e-commerce platform is a website or application that enables businesses to display and sell products or services online.
It is important because it allows customers to view products, place orders and make payments online.
It helps a business reach more customers and sell beyond its local area.
solutions.answer: An e-commerce platform enables online buying and selling and helps a business reach more customers.

solutions.question: Why is it important to identify market needs when generating a business idea?
steps: Identifying market needs helps an entrepreneur understand the problems, wants and preferences of potential customers.
A business idea that meets a real market need is more likely to attract customers and succeed.
It also helps avoid investing time and money in products or services for which there is little demand.
solutions.answer: Identifying market needs helps an entrepreneur develop an idea that customers want and are willing to buy.

solutions.question: What is the main purpose of using design thinking in creative problem-solving?
steps: The main purpose of design thinking is to solve problems creatively by focusing on the needs of the people who experience them.
It involves understanding users, defining the problem, developing ideas, creating solutions and testing them.
Feedback and testing help improve the solution.
solutions.answer: Design thinking is a user-focused approach to developing and improving creative solutions to problems.

solutions.question: Explain the importance of market analysis in a business plan. Give an example relevant to a local business in Pakistan.
steps: Market analysis is the study of customers, their needs, competitors and market demand.
It helps a business identify its target customers, understand competition and decide suitable products, prices and promotion methods.
This information helps an entrepreneur judge whether a business idea is practical and plan how the business can succeed.
For example, before opening a bakery in Lahore, an entrepreneur could survey nearby residents about the types of baked goods they want and the prices they can afford.
The entrepreneur could also study nearby bakeries to understand their products and prices, then plan products that meet local demand.
solutions.answer: Market analysis helps a business understand customers, demand and competition; a Lahore bakery can use it to choose products and prices that suit local customers.

solutions.question: What are revenue models, and why are they essential components of a business plan?
steps: A revenue model explains how a business earns money from its products or services.
Examples include selling products, charging a fee for a service or receiving a subscription payment.
Revenue models are essential in a business plan because they show how the business will generate income and help assess whether it can cover its costs and remain profitable.
solutions.answer: A revenue model explains how a business earns income and shows how it can cover costs and become profitable.

solutions.question: How can businesses contribute to environmental sustainability according to the Sustainable Development Goals?
steps: Businesses can support the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by using resources responsibly and reducing waste and pollution.
They can use energy-efficient methods and renewable energy to reduce their environmental impact.
They can also reuse and recycle materials and make products in a more sustainable way.
These actions support responsible consumption and production (SDG 12) and climate action (SDG 13).
solutions.answer: Businesses contribute to environmental sustainability by conserving resources, reducing waste and pollution, and adopting sustainable production practices.

solutions.question: Explain why entrepreneurship is important for economic growth and innovation. Provide examples from the text to support your answer.
steps: Entrepreneurship is the process of identifying an opportunity, organizing resources and accepting the risk of starting or developing a business.
Entrepreneurs create employment by hiring workers and may create self-employment for themselves. For example, a person who starts a bakery may employ bakers, sales staff and delivery workers.
They introduce new or improved products, services and methods. For example, a business may develop an easier way for farmers to store or sell their produce.
Entrepreneurs use resources such as labour, capital and raw materials productively. This increases production and can raise income and the supply of goods and services.
New businesses encourage competition, which can improve quality, choice and prices for customers. Successful businesses may also expand trade and contribute to national income.
Thus, entrepreneurship supports economic growth, provides livelihoods and encourages innovation, although a business must be planned and managed carefully because it involves risk.
solutions.answer: Entrepreneurship contributes to economic growth by creating businesses, jobs and income; using resources productively; increasing the supply of goods and services; and encouraging innovation and competition. For example, a new bakery can employ local workers, while an improved agricultural service can help farmers store or sell produce more effectively.

solutions.question: Explain how market research tools, online marketing tools, and e-commerce platforms can work together to help a business succeed in the digital world.
steps: Market research tools, such as online surveys, website analytics and social-media polls, help a business understand customers, their needs and competing products.
The business uses this information to decide what to sell, who its customers are and how to price and improve its products.
Online marketing tools, such as a website, social-media pages, email and online advertisements, help the business reach and communicate with potential customers.
The business can use the findings from market research to make its online advertisements and messages relevant to the customers most likely to buy.
An e-commerce platform displays products, accepts orders and payments, and helps the business manage sales online.
Together, these tools allow a business to learn about customers, promote suitable products, make sales online and use customer feedback to improve its service.
For example, a bookstore can use a survey to learn which textbooks students need, promote those books on social media and sell them through its online store.
solutions.answer: Market research identifies customer needs, online marketing reaches customers, and e-commerce platforms turn interest into online sales.

solutions.question: Explain the design thinking process and how it can be applied to create a new product or service. Provide an example of how design thinking could be used to help farmers in rural Pakistan.
steps: Design thinking is a human-centred process for understanding people’s needs and developing and improving solutions to their problems.

Empathise: Talk to farmers in a rural area of Pakistan and observe their work to understand their difficulties, such as unreliable irrigation, changing weather or difficulty finding fair market prices.
Define: State the main problem clearly. For example: “Farmers need affordable, timely information to decide when to water their crops and where to sell them.”
Ideate: Think of several possible solutions, such as an Urdu or local-language mobile service, SMS alerts, or a simple phone helpline giving weather, irrigation and market-price information.
Prototype: Make a simple, low-cost version of the chosen service, such as a sample SMS system that sends weather and crop-price updates to a small group of farmers.
Test: Let farmers use the prototype, ask for their feedback and find out whether the information is understandable and useful. Improve the service using their suggestions, then test it again.
This process helps ensure that the final product or service is practical, affordable and suited to the farmers who will use it.
solutions.answer: Design thinking develops solutions by empathising with users, defining their problem, generating ideas, prototyping and testing; for rural Pakistani farmers, this could produce an improved Urdu SMS service for weather, irrigation and market-price information.

solutions.question: Imagine you want to start a small online bookstore catering to students in your area. Develop a comprehensive business plan for your bookstore, including. A market analysis focusing on student reading habits and competitors.
steps: Business idea: establish an online bookstore serving students in the local area, with textbooks, exam guides, past papers and affordable supplementary reading.
Target customers: students in nearby schools, colleges and tuition centres, and parents or teachers who buy books for them.
Market research: ask students and teachers which books they use, how often they buy books, what price range they can afford and whether they prefer new or used books.
Use short online surveys, conversations at schools or tuition centres, and social-media polls to collect this information.
Student reading habits: check which subjects and exam guides are most requested, when students buy books during the school year, and whether they also read novels or other books for enjoyment.
Competitor analysis: compare local bookshops and online booksellers by checking their book selection, prices, delivery areas, delivery times and customer service.
Identify an opportunity by offering convenient local delivery, clear prices and the required course books in one place.
Use the research results to choose the initial stock and update it when students’ needs change.
solutions.answer: Research local students’ reading and buying habits, compare competing booksellers, and stock the books students need at suitable prices.

solutions.question: Imagine you want to start a small online bookstore catering to students in your area. Develop a comprehensive business plan for your bookstore, including. A revenue model outlining how you will generate income.
steps: The bookstore will earn income mainly by selling books through its website or online store.
It can sell new textbooks, exam preparation books, stationery bundles and selected supplementary reading material.
Where suitable books are available, the store can also sell second-hand books at lower prices to students.
The selling price should cover the purchase cost of each book and other business costs, while remaining affordable for local students.
The store can offer delivery for an additional fee or provide free delivery for orders above a stated amount, if the delivery cost is covered.
It may offer school or tuition-centre group orders at a negotiated price to encourage larger purchases.
For example, before each school term, the store could prepare subject-wise book bundles and sell them to students who need a complete set.
The business should record sales, costs and profit regularly and adjust its stock and prices according to demand.
solutions.answer: The bookstore will earn revenue from book and bundle sales, with possible delivery charges and group orders.

solutions.question: Imagine you want to start a small online bookstore catering to students in your area. Develop a comprehensive business plan for your bookstore, including. Digital marketing strategies you will use to promote your bookstore online.
steps: Create a simple online store with clear book titles, prices, availability, delivery information and contact details.
Use social-media pages popular with local students and parents to announce new stock, discounts and examination-season offers.
Post useful content, such as reading suggestions, book lists for each class and reminders about required textbooks.
Use paid online advertisements targeted to people in the local area, where the budget allows.
Share the store’s catalogue and order information through school, tuition-centre and community groups, with permission.
Encourage satisfied customers to leave honest reviews and share their experience with other students.
Send email or messaging updates to customers who have agreed to receive them, especially when requested books become available.
Check which posts and advertisements result in enquiries and orders, then focus on the most effective methods.
solutions.answer: Promote the bookstore through a clear online store, local social media, useful book content, targeted advertisements and customer reviews.

solutions.question: Ensure your answers are detailed and include practical examples relevant to starting your bookstore in Pakistan.
steps: Before starting a bookstore in Pakistan, identify the intended customers, such as school students, teachers, university students and families.
Research the local market by visiting nearby schools and bookshops, asking customers what they need, and checking which books and stationery items are in demand.
Choose a suitable location near schools, colleges or a busy neighbourhood. Compare rent, customer access, safety and competition before deciding.
Prepare a budget for rent, shelves, books, stationery, electricity, staff and advertising. Keep some money aside for unexpected costs and for restocking popular items.

Find reliable publishers, wholesalers and local suppliers. Compare prices and delivery terms, and begin with a carefully chosen stock of textbooks, children’s books, exam guides, novels and stationery.
Complete the legal and business requirements that apply to the shop, and keep clear records of purchases, sales, expenses and stock.
Set prices carefully so the shop can cover its costs while remaining affordable. Consider offering discounts, pre-orders for school textbooks or second-hand books in good condition.
Promote the bookstore using a clear sign, school and community notices, and social media. Offer customers a way to ask about book availability, such as a phone or WhatsApp contact.

For example, a person opening a small bookstore near a school in Lahore could ask local teachers which textbooks are used, purchase those books from wholesalers before the school term, stock affordable stationery, and accept WhatsApp orders for collection at the shop.
Review sales and customer feedback regularly. Reorder books that sell well and adjust the stock and services when customers’ needs change.
solutions.answer: To start a bookstore in Pakistan, research local demand, choose a suitable location, plan the budget, arrange suppliers and legal requirements, and promote the shop; for example, a Lahore shop near a school could stock teacher-recommended textbooks and stationery and take WhatsApp orders.

solutions.question: Choose a local business in Pakistan and discuss how it aligns with one or more Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Include its impact on social, environmental, and economic sustainability.
steps: Example: A neighbourhood bookstore in Lahore can support Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4, Quality Education, and SDG 8, Decent Work and Economic Growth. It can also contribute to SDG 12, Responsible Consumption and Production.

Social sustainability: By selling textbooks and other reading materials and helping students find affordable books, the bookstore supports learning and access to education. It can also provide jobs for local people.

Environmental sustainability: The bookstore can reduce waste by reusing delivery cartons, offering reusable bags, selling second-hand books in good condition and choosing responsibly produced paper products where available.

Economic sustainability: The bookstore earns income from sales, creates local employment and can buy from publishers, wholesalers and suppliers in Pakistan. These activities help money circulate in the local economy.
The business can strengthen these contributions by keeping prices accessible, treating workers fairly and managing its stock to avoid unnecessary waste.
solutions.answer: A neighbourhood bookstore in Lahore can support SDG 4, SDG 8 and SDG 12 by improving access to books and jobs, reducing waste through reuse and second-hand books, and earning income while supporting local suppliers.

definitions.text: Entrepreneurship is the process of designing, launching, and running a new business, often initially a small business, offering a product, process, or service for sale or hire. It involves the willingness to take risks and innovate in order to create value.

Entrepreneurship is the process of starting a new business or organization. It involves identifying a need in the market, coming up with an idea to meet that need, and taking the risk to bring that idea to life.
The word "entrepreneur" comes from a French word that means "to undertake." Entrepreneurs undertake the task of starting and running new businesses.
Innovation means creating something new or improving something that already exists.
Digital entrepreneurship involves leveraging the power of the Internet, digital platforms, and various technologies to create and run businesses.
Digital marketing involves promoting products and services using digital channels
e-commerce refers to buying and selling goods online.

Identifying market needs and opportunities is the first step in generating a viable business idea. Understanding what people need or want can help you create products or services that fulfill those needs.

A business plan is a detailed document that outlines your business goals and the strategies you will use to achieve them. It serves as a blueprint for your business, helping you to stay organized and focused.

Market analysis involves researching your target market to understand the needs and preferences of your potential customers. This includes studying market trends, analyzing competitors, and identifying your target audience.
A revenue model outlines how your business will generate income. This includes pricing strategies, sales forecasts, and potential revenue streams.
Sustainable growth focuses on developing a business that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a set of 17 global goals established by the United Nations to address various social, economic, and environmental challenges.
Reducing carbon footprints, using renewable resources, and minimizing waste.

For the online-bookstore business plan, use the three requested headings: market analysis, revenue model, and digital marketing strategies. Answer every sub-part rather than writing one general paragraph.
In market analysis, name the target customers and explain what you would find out about their needs, reading habits, market trends, and competitors.
In the revenue model, state clearly how the bookstore will earn income; include pricing, sales forecasts, or possible revenue streams.
For digital marketing, name suitable channels such as social media, search engines, and email, and say how they will help promote the bookstore.

Use clear headings and complete sentences. Give a practical Pakistan-based example and finish with a short statement linking your points back to the question.
mistakes: Writing that entrepreneurship only means owning a business. Fix: explain starting and running a business, identifying a need, and taking a risk to bring an idea to life.
Listing digital tools without explaining their benefit. Fix: connect them to reaching customers, improving operations, or selling to a global audience.
Describing market analysis as only checking competitors. Fix: also mention target customers, their needs and preferences, and market trends.
Giving a bookstore revenue model that only describes advertising or promotion. Fix: state plainly how it earns income and include pricing, sales forecasts, or revenue streams.

Giving examples that do not support the point being made. Fix: link each example directly to entrepreneurship, market analysis, revenue, marketing, or sustainability.

practicals.label: Activity 1.01
practicals.bookText:
Classroom Discussion, Brainstorming, and System Mapping
Objective: To introduce the concept of systems and understand how different components interact within a system.
Required Material: Poster boards, markers, sticky notes, chart paper, drawing tools.
Activity Type: Group
Activity Tasks Detail: Start with a discussion where the teacher introduces the concept of systems using examples like cars and schools. Students will contribute their examples and ideas. Next perform, a brainstorming session, where students will work in groups to identify and list the systems they interact with daily. They will then create a system map on poster boards, labeling the components and their interactions. Finally, during a gallery walk, each group will present their system map, followed by a feedback session where the teacher provides feedback and answers questions.
Output: Each group will produce a system map poster illustrating their chosen system, and students will enhance their presentation and explanation skills.
procedure: The teacher introduces the concept of systems using examples like cars and schools.
Contribute examples and ideas during the discussion.
Work in groups to identify and list the systems you interact with daily.
Choose a system and create a system map on a poster board, labeling its components and their interactions.
During a gallery walk, present your group’s system map.
Take part in the feedback session; listen to the teacher’s feedback and ask or answer questions.
practicals.aim: To understand systems and how different components interact within a system by creating and presenting a system map.

viva.question: What is a system?
viva.answer: A system is a set of interacting components that work together.

viva.question: Name one example of a system.
viva.answer: A school is an example of a system.

viva.question: What does a system map show?
viva.answer: It shows a system’s components and the interactions between them.

viva.question: Why are interactions included in a system map?
viva.answer: They show how the components affect or connect with one another.

viva.question: What is a gallery walk?
viva.answer: It is an activity in which groups view and present their work to one another.

practicals.diagram: Draw a system map of the group’s chosen system on a poster board; label the system, each component, and the arrows showing interactions between components.
practicals.title: System Mapping
precautions: Make sure each component in the map is clearly labelled.
Use arrows clearly to show interactions between components.
Keep the poster layout neat and easy to read.
Listen respectfully to other groups during presentations and feedback.
practicals.result: The group produced and presented a system map showing the components of its chosen system and their interactions.

practicals.label: Activity 1.02
practicals.bookText:
Design a Simple System
Objective: To apply the principles of system design and understand the process of creating a functional system.
Required Material: Computers or tablets with diagramming software (e.g., Lucidchart), paper, pencils, markers.
Activity Type: Pair
Activity Tasks Detail: Begin with an introduction where the teacher presents an example of a simple system. Students will then work in pairs to define the objective of their chosen system, list its components, describe their interactions, and outline the system's environment. The pairs will use diagramming software to create a system prototype or diagram. Finally, they will present their designs to the class in a review and feedback session.
Output: Each pair will produce a system prototype or diagram and receive feedback to refine their design ideas.
procedure: Listen to the teacher’s introduction and example of a simple system.
Work in pairs and choose a system to design.
Define the objective of the chosen system.
List the system’s components.
Describe how the components interact.
Outline the system’s environment.
Use diagramming software to create a system prototype or diagram.
Present the design to the class and take part in the review and feedback session.
Use the feedback to refine the design.
practicals.aim: To apply the principles of system design by defining a system’s objective, components, interactions and environment, and creating a prototype or diagram.

viva.question: What is a system?
viva.answer: A set of interacting components working together to achieve an objective.

viva.question: What is the objective of a system?
viva.answer: The goal or purpose the system is designed to achieve.

viva.question: What are system components?
viva.answer: The parts that make up a system.

viva.question: What do interactions describe?
viva.answer: How the components of a system relate to or work with one another.

viva.question: What is a system’s environment?
viva.answer: The surroundings and external factors that can affect or interact with the system.

viva.question: Why is feedback useful when designing a system?
viva.answer: It helps identify improvements and refine the design.

apparatus: Computer or tablet with diagramming software
practicals.diagram: Draw a system diagram and label the system name, objective, components, interactions between components, and environment.
practicals.title: Designing a Simple System
precautions: Define the system’s objective clearly before drawing the diagram.
Include the main components needed to achieve the objective.
Show interactions between components clearly and accurately.
Label the system and its environment so the diagram is easy to understand.
Use the computer or tablet carefully and save the work.
practicals.result: A system prototype or diagram was created showing its objective, components, interactions and environment. Feedback was used to refine the design.

practicals.label: Activity 1.03
practicals.bookText:
Interactive Simulation
The purpose of this activity is with the aim of understanding how variability affects the system of interest.
Materials Needed: Computers or tablets with internet access and online simulation tools (like an ecosystem simulator).
Activity Tasks Detail: Individual or Group Assignments The teacher will begin by explaining what system dynamics entail as well as provide an overview on how the simulation will be implemented. Students will then work with the simulation tool, manipulating different variables and analyzing how the system reacts. Using an S-curve to review their results, the students will be reflecting on how changes impact the entire system during the discussion. The teacher will emphasize that all these parts are integrated and balanced, and the students will follow this aspect during their conversation.
Outcome: They produce detailed observation notes as well as better insights into system dynamics and balance.
practicals.title: Observing Variability in an Interactive Simulation
practicals.aim: To understand how variability affects a system of interest by changing variables in an interactive simulation and observing the system’s response.

practicals.label: Activity 1.04
practicals.bookText:
Simulation Game
**Objective:** To experience managing a system and making decisions to keep it functional.
**Required Material:** Computers or tablets with internet access, city simulation game (e.g., SimCity).
**Activity Type:** Pair (Group of two students)
**Activity Tasks Detail:** Begin with an introduction to the simulation game, explaining its objectives and mechanics. Students will then play the game in pairs, making strategic decisions to manage their city. After gameplay, a debriefing session will allow students to discuss their experiences, challenges, and strategies. The teacher will link these experiences to system management concepts discussed in class.
**Output:** Hands-on gameplay experience and reflection on system management challenges and strategies.
procedure: Work in pairs.
Begin with an introduction to the simulation game, including its objectives and mechanics.
Play the game with your partner, making strategic decisions to manage the city.
After gameplay, discuss your experiences, challenges, and strategies.
Relate the gameplay experience to system management concepts discussed in class.
practicals.aim: To experience managing a system and making decisions to keep it functional.

viva.question: What is a simulation game?
viva.answer: A game that models a real or imagined system for users to interact with.

viva.question: What is the objective of this activity?
viva.answer: To practise managing a system and making decisions to keep it functional.

viva.question: What does system management involve in the game?
viva.answer: Making decisions and using resources to manage the city.

viva.question: Why do students play in pairs?
viva.answer: To discuss choices and work together on city management.

viva.question: What is a debriefing session?
viva.answer: A discussion after gameplay about experiences, challenges, and strategies.

practicals.title: Managing a City with a Simulation Game
precautions: Use the computer or tablet carefully and keep it on a stable surface.
Use only the assigned simulation game and follow the teacher’s instructions.
Make decisions together with your partner and take turns using the device.
Do not share personal information while using an online game.
practicals.result: The city simulation provided hands-on experience in managing a system. We discussed the challenges and strategies involved in keeping the city functional.

practicals.label: Activity 1.05
practicals.bookText:
The Journey of Data
**Objectives:** Students will discover how computer components work together to process and display data.
**Required Material:** Markers, index cards, and a flowchart template are required.
**Pair-based activity:** Tasks. Begin with an introduction to data processing in computers. Students will work in pairs to create a flowchart illustrating the data stream from input to output. Each pair will present their flowcharts and participate in a class discussion to highlight key points.
**Output:** Improved presentation and debating skills, as well as thorough flowcharts depicting the data path.
procedure: Begin with an introduction to data processing in computers.
Work in pairs to create a flowchart illustrating the data stream from input to output.
Present the flowchart to the class.
Participate in a class discussion to highlight key points.
practicals.aim: To show how computer components work together as data moves from input to output.

viva.question: What is data processing?
viva.answer: It is the process of transforming input data into useful information.

viva.question: What is the first stage in the data stream shown in your flowchart?
viva.answer: Input.

viva.question: What happens during processing?
viva.answer: The computer works on the input data according to instructions.

viva.question: What is output?
viva.answer: The information produced by the computer after processing.

viva.question: What does an arrow in a flowchart show?
viva.answer: The direction or sequence of the flow.

practicals.diagram: Draw a flowchart with three labelled boxes—Input, Processing, and Output—joined by arrows in that order.
practicals.title: The Journey of Data
precautions: Write each flowchart label clearly.
Draw arrows to show the correct direction from input to output.
Keep the flowchart neat and easy to follow.
Listen respectfully to other pairs during presentations and discussion.
practicals.result: A flowchart was created to show the path of data from input through processing to output. The activity also helped develop presentation and discussion skills.

practicals.label: Activity 1.06
practicals.bookText:
Exploring Computer Components
**Objective:** Students will learn about the different components of a computer and their functions.
**Required Material:** Physical computer parts (CPU, RAM, etc.), diagrams of computer systems, worksheets for labeling and note-taking.
**Activity Type:** Group (Small groups of 3-4 students)
**Activity Tasks Detail:** The teacher will start with an overview of key computer components. Students will then work in small groups identifying and labeling computer parts using worksheets. Groups will present their findings in a session, followed by a Q&A where the teacher clarifies any misunderstandings.
**Output:** Labeled worksheets, enhanced presentation skills, and a deeper understanding of computer components.
procedure: Listen to the teacher’s overview of key computer components.
Work in a small group to identify the physical computer parts.
Use the diagrams of computer systems to identify and label the computer parts on the worksheet.
Present the group’s findings to the class.
Take part in the question-and-answer session and clarify any misunderstandings.
practicals.aim: To identify different computer components and learn their functions.

viva.question: What is the CPU?
viva.answer: The CPU processes instructions and controls the operations of the computer.

viva.question: What is RAM used for?
viva.answer: RAM temporarily stores data and instructions that the CPU is currently using.

viva.question: What is a computer component?
viva.answer: A computer component is a hardware part that performs a function in a computer system.

viva.question: What is the function of a monitor?
viva.answer: A monitor displays visual output from the computer.

viva.question: Name one input device.
viva.answer: A keyboard is an input device.

apparatus: Physical computer parts, including the CPU and RAM
practicals.diagram: Draw a computer system and label the CPU, RAM, monitor, keyboard, and mouse.
practicals.title: Identifying Computer Components
precautions: Handle physical computer parts carefully and by their edges.
Do not touch electrical contacts or circuit components unnecessarily.
Do not connect or disconnect computer parts while the computer is powered on.
Keep food and liquids away from the computer parts and worksheets.
practicals.result: The computer components were identified and labelled, and their functions were discussed. The group presented its findings.
