quiz.stem: You suspect a laptop battery is dead. Which action tests this theory?
options: Plug in the power cord and see whether the laptop turns on
Write down that the laptop did not turn on
Decide that the battery might be dead
rationales: This is a possible solution, not a test to determine whether the theory is correct.
This is correct because plugging in the power cord tests whether the suspected battery problem is causing the issue.
This records the problem but does not test the theory.
This establishes a theory but does not test it.

quiz.stem: What should you do after implementing a solution?
options: Establish a theory of probable cause
rationales: Documentation is the final step, after checking that the system works.
Implementing the solution is the step that comes before verification.
This is correct because you must check that the problem is resolved and the system works properly.
A theory of probable cause is established earlier in the process.

quiz.stem: Why is it useful to document troubleshooting findings, actions, and outcomes?
options: It provides a record for future reference
It guarantees that the problem will never happen again
It replaces the need to test a theory
It means the solution does not need to be checked
rationales: This is correct because the record can help with future troubleshooting of similar problems.
Documentation cannot guarantee that a problem will never happen again.
Recording information does not replace testing a suspected cause.
The system still needs to be checked after a solution is implemented.

quiz.stem: What does downtime mean?
options: A computer is running more quickly
A computer has accurate and reliable data
A computer has had its findings recorded
rationales: This is correct because downtime occurs when a computer system is not operational.
Running more quickly describes improved performance, not downtime.
Accurate and reliable data describes data integrity.
Recording findings is part of documentation, not downtime.

quiz.stem: How can troubleshooting support data integrity?
options: It helps identify data corruption and prevent it from happening again
It ensures that hardware is always up to date
It removes the need for data backups
It makes every system immune to cyber-attacks
rationales: This is correct because troubleshooting can find the source of data corruption and help prevent it from recurring.
Troubleshooting does not ensure that hardware is always up to date.
Troubleshooting does not remove the need for backups.
Troubleshooting can help identify security issues but cannot make a system immune to all attacks.

quiz.stem: An application has stopped responding. Which action does the section recommend trying first?
options: Click End Task in Task Manager.
Hold the computer’s power button as the first step.
rationales: Correct: Open Task Manager, select the unresponsive application, and click End Task.
Incorrect: Reinstalling is a possible later step if the problem persists, not the first recommended action.
Incorrect: A forced shutdown is a last resort and may cause data loss.
Incorrect: Deleting application files is not the recommended way to handle a freeze.

quiz.stem: A connected keyboard is not responding. Which troubleshooting sequence best follows the section?
options: Leave the device plugged in and wait.
Check the connection, unplug and reconnect it, and consider updating its driver.
rationales: Incorrect: Waiting alone does not check the likely connection or software causes.
Correct: Check that the connection is secure, reconnect the device, and update its driver if needed.
Incorrect: A hard drive replacement is unrelated to a peripheral connection problem.
Incorrect: Disabling updates does not address an unresponsive keyboard.

quiz.stem: Which action is an example of identifying a problem?
options: A plan to replace the battery.
A laptop does not turn on when the power button is pressed.
A record that a battery was replaced.
rationales: Incorrect: This is a plan of action, not identifying the issue.
Correct: Noticing and defining the failure to turn on identifies the problem.
Incorrect: This documents an action that has already happened.
Incorrect: This tests a possible cause.

quiz.stem: Which action should generally be used only as a last resort because it can cause data loss?
options: Clicking Task Manager’s End Task option.
Using Ctrl + Alt + Delete to open Task Manager.
Holding the power button to force shutdown.
rationales: Incorrect: Ending an unresponsive application through Task Manager is a recommended software fix.
Incorrect: This opens Task Manager and is part of the recommended response to a frozen application.
Correct: A forced shutdown can cause data loss if programs are not properly closed.
Incorrect: Updating software is a routine maintenance step.

quiz.stem: Which group of symptoms is associated with possible RAM failure?
options: A loose cable and no display.
Clicking noises, slow performance, and corrupted files.
rationales: Correct: Frequent crashes, BSODs, poor performance, failure to boot, or random restarts can indicate RAM issues.
Incorrect: A loose cable or display problem does not specifically identify RAM failure.
Incorrect: Clicking noises and corrupted files are listed as possible hard drive symptoms.
Incorrect: A missing keyboard driver is a peripheral software issue, not a RAM symptom.

quiz.stem: Which tools can help monitor hard drive health?
rationales: Correct: The section names SMART status checks and CrystalDiskInfo for hard drive health.
Incorrect: Windows Memory Diagnostic checks RAM, not hard drive health.
Incorrect: Cable ties and labels help organize cables.
Incorrect: End Task closes an unresponsive application.

quiz.stem: Which choice gives two backup methods described in the section?
options: Store files only on the computer’s internal drive.
Use an external drive or USB flash drive, or use cloud storage.
Delete all files after each use.
Keep the computer running all the time.
rationales: Incorrect: Keeping files only on the internal drive does not create a separate backup.
Correct: External storage and cloud services are both described backup methods.
Incorrect: Deleting files is not a backup method and may cause data loss.
Incorrect: Leaving a computer on does not make a backup.

quiz.stem: Which is the best practice for creating a strong password according to the section?
options: Use a mixture of upper- and lower-case letters, numbers, and special characters.
Use only a short word that is easy to remember.
Use the same password everywhere and never change it.
Write the password in a public place.
rationales: Correct: The section recommends combining upper- and lower-case letters, numbers, and special characters.
Incorrect: A short, simple word is easier to guess.
Incorrect: The section advises changing passwords regularly and managing them carefully.
Incorrect: A public password note can expose the account to unauthorized access.

quiz.stem: What is the primary function of an operating system?
options: To manage hardware resources and provide a user interface
rationales: Creating documents is a task performed by application software, not the operating system’s primary function.
Correct: An operating system manages hardware resources and provides an interface through which users interact with the computer.
Performing calculations is a task handled by applications or hardware, not the operating system’s primary function.
Designing graphics is typically done with application software, not an operating system.

quiz.stem: Which software is used to enhance system performance and security?
rationales: An operating system manages the computer’s resources, but utility software is specifically used for tasks such as maintenance and security.
Correct: Utility software helps maintain, protect, and improve a computer system.
Application software helps users perform specific tasks, rather than primarily improving system performance and security.
Device drivers enable the operating system to communicate with hardware, but they are not the general category of software used for system maintenance and security.

quiz.stem: What role do device drivers play in a computer system?
options: Facilitate communication between hardware devices and the operating system
rationales: Managing files is usually handled by the operating system or file-management utilities, not the primary role of device drivers.
Correct: Device drivers allow the operating system to communicate with and control hardware devices.
Creating presentations is a task performed by application software.
Some drivers can affect graphics performance, but their general role is to enable communication between hardware and the operating system.

quiz.stem: Which of the following is an example of application software?
rationales: Correct: Microsoft Word is application software used to create and edit documents.
BIOS is firmware that initializes hardware and helps start the computer, not application software.
Disk Cleanup is a system utility used to remove unnecessary files, not application software.
Device Manager is an operating-system tool for managing hardware and drivers, not application software.

quiz.stem: What is the main purpose of a spreadsheet software?
rationales: Editing text documents is primarily the purpose of word-processing software.
Correct: Spreadsheet software organizes data in rows and columns and supports analysis using formulas and other tools.
Creating visual content is more commonly done with graphics or presentation software.
Enhancing system security is a function of security utilities, not spreadsheet software.

quiz.stem: How does utility software differ from application software?
options: Utility software manages hardware, while application software performs specific tasks for users.
Utility software creates documents, while application software manages hardware.
Utility software performs specific tasks for users, while application software manages hardware.
Utility software is free, while application software is paid.
rationales: Correct: Utility software helps maintain or manage the computer system, while application software helps users perform specific tasks.
Creating documents is generally a task of application software, and managing hardware is primarily an operating-system function.
This reverses the usual distinction: applications perform user tasks, while utilities support system maintenance.
Utility software is not defined by being free, and application software may be either free or paid.

quiz.stem: Which type of software would you use to design a logo?
rationales: An operating system manages the computer and does not specialize in logo design.
Spreadsheet software is designed for organizing and analyzing data, not creating logos.
Correct: Graphic design software provides tools for creating and editing visual designs such as logos.
Utility software supports system maintenance and performance rather than graphic design.

quiz.stem: What is the function of system software?
options: To facilitate communication between hardware and software
To perform specific tasks for the user
rationales: Correct: System software, including operating systems and drivers, helps coordinate communication between hardware and software.
Performing specific tasks for users is primarily the role of application software.
Creating visual content is a task for graphics applications, not system software.
Organizing and analyzing data is commonly done with spreadsheet application software.

quiz.stem: Why are operating system updates important?
options: They enhance security and fix bugs
rationales: Increasing screen brightness is a display setting and is not the main purpose of operating-system updates.
Adding fonts may occur in some updates, but it is not their general importance.
Correct: Updates commonly address security vulnerabilities and fix bugs.
Updates may sometimes affect battery performance, but improving battery life is not their primary purpose.

quiz.stem: What is a common task you can perform using word processing software?
rationales: Correct: Word-processing software is used to create, edit, and format text documents.
Managing hardware resources is primarily the operating system’s role.
Enhancing system performance is generally the purpose of utility software.
Organizing and analyzing data is a common task for spreadsheet software.

quiz.stem: Which statement best describes software?
options: A collection of programs and instructions
rationales: This is correct because software is a collection of programs and instructions.
This describes hardware, not software.
A screen is a hardware component, not software.
A list of websites is not the definition of software.

quiz.stem: What is the main purpose of application software?
options: It helps users perform specific tasks
It only protects the computer from viruses
It is always a physical part of the computer
It replaces the need for system software
rationales: This is correct because application software is designed to help users perform specific tasks.
Virus protection is one possible utility function, not the purpose of all application software.
Application software is made of programs, not physical computer parts.
Application software runs on a platform provided by system software; it does not replace it.

quiz.stem: Which of these is system software?
rationales: This is correct because Linux is an example of an operating system, which is system software.
Google Docs is a word processor, an example of application software.
Minecraft is a game, an example of application software.
VLC Media Player is a media player, an example of application software.

quiz.stem: Which item is an example of a device driver?
rationales: This is correct because printer drivers are listed as examples of device drivers.
A web browser is application software.
A word processor is application software.
A computer game is application software.

quiz.stem: Which item is an example of a utility program?
rationales: This is correct because disk cleanup tools are listed as utility programs.
A presentation is content created using application software, not a utility program.
A web page is content viewed or created using applications, not a utility program.
A word-processing document is a file made using application software.

quiz.stem: Which statement matches the section's description of software installation?
options: System software is usually pre-installed; application software can be installed as needed.
Application software is always pre-installed; system software is installed only when needed.
Neither type can be installed on a computer.
rationales: This is correct: the section says system software is usually pre-installed and application software can be installed by the user as needed.
This reverses the installation description in the section.
The section does not say that both types are always pre-installed.
The section says application software can be installed by the user.

quiz.stem: Which statement best describes the role of an operating system?
options: It manages hardware and software and provides an interface for users.
It translates documents into another language.
rationales: This is correct because an operating system manages hardware and software and provides a way for users and applications to interact with the computer.
This is incorrect because creating documents is a task of application software.
This is incorrect because virus scanning is a function of antivirus utility software.
This is incorrect because document translation is not the operating system's main role.

quiz.stem: Which type of user interface uses windows, icons and menus?
rationales: This is incorrect because a command-line interface requires users to type text commands.
This is correct because a graphical user interface uses visual elements such as windows, icons and menus.
This is incorrect because backup is a utility function, not one of the two user-interface types described.
This is incorrect because a device driver helps hardware communicate with the operating system; it is not this type of user interface.

quiz.stem: Which interface requires the user to type text commands?
rationales: This is incorrect because a GUI uses visual elements such as icons and menus.
This is correct because a command-line interface requires users to type commands.
This is incorrect because a backup program copies files or folders for recovery.
This is incorrect because a printer driver enables communication with a printer.

quiz.stem: Which utility scans for temporary and other unnecessary files that can safely be deleted?
rationales: This is correct because Disk Cleanup scans for temporary, cached and other unnecessary files.
This is incorrect because antivirus software scans for viruses and malware.
This is incorrect because backup software saves copies of files and folders for later recovery.
This is incorrect because file compression tools reduce file size and can place files in an archive.

quiz.stem: What does a printer driver do?
options: It checks the printer for viruses.
It translates computer instructions into instructions the printer can understand.
It creates a backup of printed documents.
rationales: This is incorrect because virus scanning is a task of antivirus software.
This is correct because a printer driver helps the computer send the correct signals to the printer.
This is incorrect because a printer driver does not create backups.
This is incorrect because compressing files is not the printer driver's role.

quiz.stem: When several applications run at the same time, how does the operating system help them run?
options: To allocate CPU time and memory to applications
To scan email attachments for malware
rationales: This is correct because the operating system manages resources such as CPU time and memory for applications.
This is incorrect because changing wallpaper is not the resource-management function described.
This is incorrect because creating archives is a function of file compression tools.
This is incorrect because scanning for malware is a function of antivirus software.

quiz.stem: Which action is an example of using backup software?
options: A regular copy of files to cloud storage
rationales: This is incorrect because a ZIP archive is made using file compression tools.
This is incorrect because real-time protection is a function of antivirus software.
This is correct because backup software can schedule copies of files to cloud storage or another location.
This is incorrect because a driver update helps a hardware device work with the operating system.

quiz.stem: Why might someone compress a large folder before emailing it?
options: To reduce file size and make transfer easier
To allocate CPU time to a file
To scan files for known malware signatures
rationales: This is correct because compression reduces file size and can make uploading and sending easier and quicker.
This is incorrect because allocating CPU time is managed by the operating system.
This is incorrect because installing an operating system is not the purpose of file compression.
This is incorrect because scanning for malware is a function of antivirus software.

quiz.stem: Which task is word processing software designed to help users perform?
rationales: Correct: word processing software is used to create and edit text documents.
Incorrect: managing hardware resources is a system software function.
Incorrect: system utilities are commonly used for security and maintenance.
Incorrect: device drivers facilitate communication between hardware and the operating system.

quiz.stem: Which application is a word processor?
rationales: Correct: Google Docs is a web-based word processor.
Incorrect: Google Sheets is spreadsheet software.
Incorrect: Adobe Illustrator is a vector graphics editor.
Incorrect: LibreOffice Calc is spreadsheet software.

quiz.stem: What is a main purpose of spreadsheet software?
options: Organizing and analyzing data in tabular form
rationales: Incorrect: creating and editing documents is the main use of word processing software.
Correct: spreadsheet software organizes, analyzes, and stores data in tabular form.
Incorrect: managing hardware is not the purpose of spreadsheet software.
Incorrect: communicating with a printer is not the main purpose of spreadsheet software.

quiz.stem: Which program is an example of spreadsheet software?
rationales: Correct: Microsoft Excel is spreadsheet software.
Incorrect: Apple Pages is a word processing application.
Incorrect: CorelDRAW is a vector graphics editor.
Incorrect: Google Docs is a word processor.

quiz.stem: Which task is best suited to graphic design software?
rationales: Correct: graphic design software can be used to create logos and illustrations.
Incorrect: system updates are handled by the operating system or update tools.
Incorrect: organizing files and folders is not a main graphic design function.
Incorrect: writing device drivers is not a graphic design task.

quiz.stem: Which application is a vector graphics editor?
rationales: Correct: Adobe Illustrator is a vector graphics editor.
Incorrect: Google Sheets is spreadsheet software.
Incorrect: Apple Pages is word processing software.
Incorrect: LibreOffice Writer is word processing software.

quiz.stem: Which feature of Google Docs is described in the section?
options: Multiple users can edit a document at the same time.
It can only be used without internet access.
It is designed mainly to create spreadsheets.
rationales: Correct: Google Docs allows real-time collaboration by multiple users.
Incorrect: the section describes Google Docs as web-based and available with internet access.
Incorrect: Google Docs is a word processor, not a device driver.
Incorrect: creating spreadsheets is the role of spreadsheet software.

quiz.stem: How is data arranged in a spreadsheet?
options: Cells arranged in rows and columns
Hardware devices arranged in a network
rationales: Correct: a spreadsheet has a grid of cells arranged in rows and columns.
Incorrect: paragraphs on pages describe text documents, not the spreadsheet grid.
Incorrect: a spreadsheet is not an arrangement of hardware devices.
Incorrect: spreadsheets can contain data and charts, not only pictures arranged by size.

quiz.stem: What is the primary objective of computer networks?
options: Enable resource sharing and data communication
rationales: Increasing computational power can be a benefit of distributed systems, but it is not the primary objective of computer networks.
Computer networks primarily enable devices to share resources and communicate data.
Enhancing graphic capabilities is not a primary objective of computer networks.
Improving software development is not a primary objective of computer networks.

quiz.stem: Which device is used to connect multiple networks and direct data packets between them?
rationales: A switch connects devices within a network, rather than routing packets between different networks.
A hub broadcasts signals among connected devices and does not direct packets between networks.
A router connects networks and forwards data packets between them.
A modem converts signals for transmission over a communication medium and does not primarily route packets between networks.

quiz.stem: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for node-to-node data transfer and error detection?
rationales: The Physical Layer transmits raw bits over a physical medium and does not provide node-to-node error detection.
The Data Link Layer handles node-to-node data transfer and performs error detection on frames.
The Network Layer routes packets between networks rather than handling node-to-node frame transfer.
The Transport Layer provides end-to-end communication between hosts rather than node-to-node transfer.

quiz.stem: What is the function of the Domain Name System (DNS)?
options: Translate domain names to IP addresses
rationales: Dynamic IP address assignment is typically performed by DHCP, not DNS.
DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
DNS does not itself secure data communication.
DNS resolves domain names, not monitors network traffic.

quiz.stem: Which method of data transmission uses a dedicated communication path?
rationales: Packet switching shares network links among packets and does not reserve a dedicated path for the entire communication.
Circuit switching establishes a dedicated communication path for the duration of a connection.
Full-duplex describes simultaneous two-way communication, not whether a path is dedicated.
Half-duplex describes two-way communication that occurs in one direction at a time, not a dedicated path.

quiz.stem: What is encapsulation in the context of network communication?
options: Converting data into a secure format
Translating domain names to IP addresses
rationales: Converting data into a secure format is encryption, not encapsulation.
Encapsulation wraps data with protocol information, such as headers and sometimes trailers, as it passes through network layers.
Monitoring network traffic is a network management or security function, not encapsulation.
Translating domain names to IP addresses is performed by DNS, not encapsulation.

quiz.stem: Which protocol is used for reliable data transfer in the TCP/IP model?
rationales: HTTP is an application-layer protocol and relies on another protocol for reliable transport.
FTP is an application-layer file-transfer protocol and typically relies on TCP for reliable transport.
TCP provides reliable, ordered data transfer in the TCP/IP model.
UDP provides connectionless transport without guaranteeing reliable delivery.

quiz.stem: What is the main purpose of a firewall in network security?
options: Convert data into a secure format
rationales: A firewall may support secure communication policies, but its main purpose is not to convert data into a secure format.
A firewall monitors and controls network traffic according to security rules.
Assigning IP addresses is generally handled by DHCP rather than a firewall.
Translating domain names is performed by DNS rather than a firewall.

quiz.stem: Which network topology connects all devices to a central hub?
rationales: In a ring topology, devices connect in a circular arrangement rather than to a central hub.
A mesh topology connects devices with multiple interconnections rather than through one central hub.
In a bus topology, devices share a common backbone cable rather than connecting to a central hub.
In a star topology, each device connects to a central hub or switch.

quiz.stem: What is a key benefit of using computer networks in businesses?
options: Enable resource sharing and efficient communication
rationales: Networks can distribute computing tasks, but increased computational power is not the key general business benefit listed here.
Networks let businesses share resources and communicate efficiently, supporting collaboration and productivity.
Enhancing graphic capabilities is not a key general business benefit of computer networks.
Improving software development may be enabled by collaboration, but it is not the key general benefit described here.

quiz.stem: In a computer network, what is a node?
options: A device connected to a network
A program used to send email
rationales: Correct: a node is a device connected to the network.
A connection is a link, not a node.
The section defines nodes as devices, not programs.
A node is a network component, not an objective.

quiz.stem: Which option describes a network link?
options: A wired or wireless connection between nodes
A device that connects different networks
rationales: Correct: links connect nodes and may be wired or wireless.
A computer that stores files is a device, not a link.
A router connects different networks.
A printer may be a network node or shared resource, not a link.

quiz.stem: What is a router's role in a computer network?
options: Connect different networks and direct data packets
Forward data only to the port for a destination MAC address
Provide storage for all network files
Connect a computer to a printer with a cable
rationales: Correct: routers connect different networks and direct data packets between them.
This describes how a switch forwards packets within a network.
The section does not identify storage as a router's role.
A cable is a link; connecting one computer to a printer is not the router's defined role.

quiz.stem: Which statement best describes a switch?
options: It connects multiple nodes within a network to forward data
It connects different networks and directs data packets
It replaces the need for all links
It creates the data being sent
rationales: Correct: a switch connects multiple nodes within a network to forward data.
This is the role of a router.
Switches do not replace the connections between nodes.
A switch forwards data; it does not create the message.

quiz.stem: Which is an example of resource sharing through a network?
options: Sharing one printer among several computers
Giving every employee a separate printer
rationales: Correct: multiple computers can share a single printer through a network.
Separate printers do not demonstrate sharing a resource.
Disconnecting devices prevents network sharing.
Stopping communication goes against a network's objectives.

quiz.stem: Which statement about the Internet is correct?
options: The Internet is a single printer shared by offices
The Internet is a type of network link
The Internet is a device that forwards data only within one network
rationales: Correct: the section describes the Internet as the largest network, connecting networks worldwide.
The Internet is not a printer.
The Internet is a network, not an individual link.
Forwarding data within one network describes a switch, not the Internet.

quiz.stem: Which component is a computer sending an email?
options: The path through which data travels
rationales: Correct: the computer is sending the data, so it is the sender.
Incorrect: the receiver is the device that gets the data.
Incorrect: the message is the email content, not the computer.
Incorrect: the medium is the path used to carry the data.

quiz.stem: A smartphone gets an email sent from a computer. What is the smartphone in this communication?
rationales: Incorrect: the sender is the device that sends the data.
Correct: the smartphone receives the email, so it is the receiver.
Incorrect: the message is the email content.
Incorrect: a protocol is a set of communication rules.

quiz.stem: In an email communication, which option is the message?
rationales: Incorrect: this is the sender.
Incorrect: this is the receiver.
Correct: the content being communicated is the message.
Incorrect: Wi-Fi is an example of a medium.

quiz.stem: What is a protocol?
options: A set of rules governing data communication
rationales: Correct: a protocol is a set of rules governing data communication.
Incorrect: this describes the sender.
Incorrect: this describes the message.
Incorrect: this describes the medium.

quiz.stem: An Ethernet cable carries data between devices. Which component does the cable represent?
rationales: Incorrect: the sender is the device that sends the data.
Incorrect: the receiver is the device that gets the data.
Correct: the cable is a path through which data travels, so it is the medium.
Incorrect: the message is the data being communicated.

quiz.stem: Which component determines the rules followed during data communication?
rationales: Incorrect: the receiver gets the data but does not define the communication rules.
Correct: the protocol is the set of rules governing communication.
Incorrect: the message is the data being communicated.
Incorrect: the sender is the device that sends the data.

quiz.stem: Which option is an example of a communication medium?
rationales: Correct: Wi-Fi is a wireless path through which data can travel.
Incorrect: email content is an example of a message.
Incorrect: the smartphone is an example of a receiver.
Incorrect: HTTP is an example of a protocol.

quiz.stem: Which list gives the five basic components of data communication?
options: Sender, receiver, message, protocol, and medium
Sender, message, router, protocol, and address
Receiver, message, cable, network, and address
Sender, receiver, software, cable, and password
rationales: Correct: these are the five basic components listed in the section.
Incorrect: router and address are not listed as two of the five basic components.
Incorrect: cable is an example of a medium, while network and address are not components in the list.
Incorrect: software and password are not included in the five-component list.

quiz.stem: How does a switch usually forward a packet after it has learned devices’ addresses?
options: It sends every packet to every connected device.
It uses destination MAC addresses to forward data to the intended device.
It assigns SIM cards to computers.
It connects only wireless devices to the internet.
rationales: This is incorrect because the switch forwards data only to the device with the matching destination MAC address.
This is correct because a switch reads the destination MAC address and sends the packet to the matching device.
This is incorrect because a SIM card identifies a subscriber on a mobile network and is not assigned by a switch.
This is incorrect because a switch connects multiple network devices and is not limited to wireless devices.

quiz.stem: Which statement best describes the role of a router?
options: It interconnects networks and directs data packets between them.
It translates domain names into MAC addresses.
It connects only printers within one network.
It transmits data only through radio waves.
rationales: This is correct because routers interconnect networks and direct packets between them.
This is incorrect because the section does not describe a router as translating domain names into MAC addresses.
This is incorrect because connecting devices within a network is associated with a switch, and routers are not limited to printers.
This is incorrect because transmitting data wirelessly is part of an access point’s role, not the router’s only role.

quiz.stem: What does a router use to help decide the best path for data packets?
options: A hardware address used by a device
A list of possible routes used by a router
A cable connecting an access point to a computer
rationales: This is incorrect because the section identifies a MAC address as a device’s hardware address used by a switch.
This is correct because a routing table lists possible paths and helps a router choose an efficient route.
This is incorrect because an Ethernet cable is a connection medium, not a list of paths.
This is incorrect because a mobile subscription does not provide the router with a list of packet routes.

quiz.stem: What is the main role of an Access Point (AP)?
options: It connects wireless devices to a wired network.
It assigns MAC addresses to routers.
It replaces the need for all network devices.
It sends packets only between different networks.
rationales: This is correct because an access point facilitates wireless devices’ connection to a wired network.
This is incorrect because the section does not say that access points assign MAC addresses.
This is incorrect because an access point is itself a networking device and does not replace all other devices.
This is incorrect because directing packets between different networks is the router’s role.

quiz.stem: How does an access point send data to wireless devices?
options: It receives data from the wired network and transmits it wirelessly to devices.
It changes wireless devices into wired devices.
It uses destination MAC addresses to choose a route between networks.
rationales: This is correct because an access point receives wired-network data and transmits it wirelessly to devices.
This is incorrect because the section describes transmitting and receiving data, not permanently storing every packet.
This is incorrect because an access point connects wireless devices to a wired network; it does not change the devices themselves.
This is incorrect because forwarding by destination MAC address within a network describes a switch.

quiz.stem: Which statement about a switch is correct?
options: A switch works at the Data Link layer and uses MAC addresses.
A switch works only through a SIM card.
A switch uses radio waves to connect wireless devices to a wired network.
A switch finds the best path between different networks.
rationales: This is correct because the section places the switch at Layer 2, the Data Link layer, and says it uses MAC addresses.

quiz.stem: Pseudocode is:
options: A high-level description of an algorithm using plain language
rationales: Incorrect: a flowchart is a graphical representation, while pseudocode is written text.
Correct: pseudocode describes an algorithm in plain, programming-like language without requiring a specific programming language.
Incorrect: pseudocode is not executable code in a programming language.
Incorrect: pseudocode describes an algorithm rather than serving as a debugging tool.

quiz.stem: Dry running a flowchart involves:
options: Writing the code in a programming language
Testing the flowchart with sample data
rationales: Incorrect: writing program code is not what dry-running a flowchart means.
Correct: dry-running traces a flowchart using sample data to check its logic.
Incorrect: converting a flowchart into pseudocode is not a dry run.
Incorrect: a dry run examines the flowchart’s steps rather than ignoring them.

quiz.stem: A student divides the task of organizing a school event into choosing a date, booking a place, and inviting guests. Which computational-thinking component is being used?
options: Breaking a complex task into smaller tasks
Hiding complex details and showing necessary parts
Following a precise sequence of instructions
rationales: This is correct because decomposition divides a complex problem into smaller, manageable tasks.
This is incorrect because pattern recognition looks for similarities or regularities.
This is incorrect because abstraction focuses on necessary details and hides complex details.
This is incorrect because an algorithm is a sequence of instructions, not the act of splitting a task.

quiz.stem: A student notices that several maths problems can be solved using the same method. Which component helps the student notice this?
rationales: This is incorrect because decomposition breaks a problem into smaller parts.
This is correct because pattern recognition involves finding similarities or regularities among problems.
This is incorrect because abstraction focuses on essential details rather than identifying similarities.
This is incorrect because an algorithm is a sequence of instructions for a task.

quiz.stem: Which action best shows abstraction?
options: Keeping every detail in the problem
Focusing on necessary details and hiding complex details
Dividing the problem into smaller tasks
Writing instructions in a programming language
rationales: This is incorrect because abstraction leaves out unnecessary details rather than keeping every detail.
This is correct because abstraction hides complex details while exposing the necessary parts.
This is incorrect because dividing a problem into smaller tasks is decomposition.
This is incorrect because abstraction is not defined as writing code in a programming language.

quiz.stem: Which description best fits an algorithm?
options: A precise sequence of instructions to achieve a specific goal
rationales: This is incorrect because a list of materials alone does not give instructions in order.
This is correct because an algorithm is a precise sequence of instructions for a goal.
This is incorrect because a picture alone is not necessarily a sequence of instructions.
This is incorrect because repeated patterns are not the definition of an algorithm.

quiz.stem: Which is an example of computational thinking being used outside computer science?
options: Planning a trip by writing clear steps
Ignoring the goal of a task
rationales: This is correct because computational thinking can help solve everyday problems such as planning a trip.
This is incorrect because computational thinking requires working toward a problem's solution.
This is incorrect because computational thinking aims to make complex problems more manageable.
This is incorrect because computational thinking is not limited to mathematical calculations.

quiz.stem: A student compares the areas of squares with side lengths 1, 2, 3, and 4. Which pattern should the student notice?
options: The area increases by 1 each time
The area can be found by adding consecutive odd numbers
The area stays the same as the side length
The area decreases as the side length increases
rationales: This is incorrect because the areas are 1, 4, 9, and 16, so they do not increase by 1.
This is correct because the areas are sums of consecutive odd numbers: 1, 1 + 3, 1 + 3 + 5, and 1 + 3 + 5 + 7.
This is incorrect because the areas are not equal to the side lengths except when the side length is 1.
This is incorrect because the area increases as the side length increases.

quiz.stem: Which item is most clearly an algorithm for baking a cake?
options: A recipe with steps in order
A drawing of a finished cake
A description of why cakes are popular
rationales: This is correct because an ordered list of steps gives instructions for achieving the goal.
This is incorrect because a picture of the result does not explain the steps to make it.
This is incorrect because a list of flavours does not give instructions for baking.
This is incorrect because an explanation of popularity does not describe how to bake a cake.

quiz.stem: Which statement about computational thinking is supported by this section?
options: It is only useful when writing computer programs
It can help with problem-solving in fields and situations beyond computer science
It means ignoring all details of a problem
It is another name for pattern recognition
rationales: This is incorrect because the section says computational thinking is used in many fields and daily life.
This is correct because computational thinking can be used in fields such as biology and mathematics and in everyday problem-solving.
This is incorrect because only abstraction hides unnecessary details, and computational thinking has other components too.
This is incorrect because pattern recognition is only one component of computational thinking.

quiz.stem: Which action best shows problem understanding?
options: Identifying the core issue, requirements, and objectives
Starting to code before considering the requirements
Choosing a solution without checking the problem
Focusing only on details unrelated to the goal
rationales: This is correct because understanding a problem includes identifying its core issue, requirements, and objectives.
This is incorrect because coding before understanding requirements can lead to an unsuitable solution.
This is incorrect because a solution should be chosen after the problem is understood.
This is incorrect because problem understanding helps focus on relevant details.

quiz.stem: What is the purpose of problem simplification?
options: It removes the need to define a goal.
It divides a problem into smaller, manageable sub-problems.
It makes every problem more complicated.
rationales: This is incorrect because simplification does not remove the need for a goal.
This is correct because the section describes simplification as breaking a problem into smaller, manageable sub-problems.
This is incorrect because simplification is intended to make a problem more manageable.
This is incorrect because solution design requires a plan, not guesswork.

quiz.stem: What does solution selection involve?
options: Evaluate different approaches and select an efficient one.
Ignore the requirements once they have been listed.
Begin with random actions and hope one works.
Avoid making a plan for the solution.
rationales: This is correct because solution selection means evaluating approaches and choosing an efficient one.
This is incorrect because the requirements guide the choice of solution.
This is incorrect because random actions are not a structured way to solve a problem.
This is incorrect because designing a solution requires a detailed plan or algorithm.

quiz.stem: In the school website example, which action helps identify requirements?
options: Making a list of possible website colours only
Finding out which pages the website needs
Writing code without knowing who will use the website
Selecting tools without checking what resources are available
rationales: This is incorrect because colours alone do not establish the website's required features.
This is correct because identifying required pages, such as news and schedules, is part of identifying requirements.
This is incorrect because the example says to understand the users before designing a user-friendly interface.
This is incorrect because checking available resources and tools is part of understanding technical constraints.

quiz.stem: How does proper problem understanding help define goals?
options: Avoiding all evaluation of possible solutions
Beginning with the final algorithm before understanding the problem
rationales: This is correct because understanding the problem helps set clear and achievable goals for the final outcome.
This is incorrect because irrelevant details distract from the problem rather than define goals.
This is incorrect because choosing an efficient solution involves evaluating approaches.
This is incorrect because understanding the problem comes before planning its solution.

quiz.stem: What does designing a solution require?
options: It creates a detailed plan or algorithm.
It guarantees that no requirements need to be checked.
It means dividing a problem into random parts.
It involves selecting an approach without considering efficiency.
rationales: This is correct because the section explains that solution design requires a detailed plan or algorithm.
This is incorrect because requirements remain important throughout solution planning.
This is incorrect because sub-problems should be manageable and related to the problem, not random.
This is incorrect because selecting a solution involves seeking an efficient approach.

quiz.stem: Which flowchart symbol represents a decision point?
rationales: An oval marks the start or end of a process, not a decision.
A rectangle represents a process, task, or operation.
A diamond represents a decision where the flow can branch.
A parallelogram represents input or output.

quiz.stem: What does an oval (terminal) represent in a flowchart?
options: It represents the start or end of a process.
It represents a task or operation.
It represents data input or output.
It shows the direction of flow.
rationales: An oval is used for the start or end of a process.
A rectangle, not an oval, represents a task or operation.
A parallelogram, not an oval, represents input or output.
An arrow (flowline), not an oval, shows the direction of flow.

quiz.stem: Which symbol is used for data input or output?
rationales: A diamond represents a decision point.
A rectangle represents a process or operation.
A parallelogram represents data input or output.
An arrow connects symbols and shows the direction of flow.

quiz.stem: Which statement best describes pseudocode?
options: It is actual code that a computer can run.
It describes an algorithm in simple, informal language.
It is a graphical representation made only of symbols.
It is used only to find errors in a program.
rationales: Pseudocode is not actual code that can be run on a computer.
Pseudocode describes algorithm steps in simple and informal language.
A flowchart, rather than pseudocode, is a graphical representation using symbols.
Pseudocode helps plan and explain algorithms; it is not only for finding errors.

quiz.stem: In the even-or-odd pseudocode, what does the condition number % 2 == 0 check?
options: Checking whether a number is divisible by 2
Testing whether a number has a divisor
rationales: It checks whether dividing the number by 2 leaves a remainder of zero.
A flowline is part of a flowchart and is not what this condition checks.
Checking possible divisors is the purpose of the prime-number example.
The condition does not choose a flowchart symbol.

quiz.stem: In the prime-number pseudocode, what happens if number <= 1?
rationales: The procedure returns False because numbers less than or equal to 1 are not prime.
It does not return True for a number less than or equal to 1.
The pseudocode does not print the number in this case.
The condition immediately returns False, so the procedure does not loop forever.

quiz.stem: What is the purpose of a flowline in a flowchart?
options: It gives each symbol a different meaning.
It connects symbols and indicates the sequence of steps.
rationales: Symbols have their meanings; a flowline does not assign those meanings.
A flowline connects symbols and shows the direction or sequence of flow.
A flowline does not replace decision symbols such as diamonds.
Input values are represented as input, not stored by a flowline.

quiz.stem: Which statement correctly differentiates pseudocode from flowcharts?
options: Pseudocode uses arrows, while flowcharts use paragraphs.
Pseudocode describes steps in structured language, while flowcharts show steps with symbols and arrows.
Pseudocode can be run directly, while flowcharts are always plain text.
There is no difference between them.
rationales: This reverses the methods: flowcharts use arrows and pseudocode uses structured language.
This correctly describes the written, structured form of pseudocode and the visual form of flowcharts.
Pseudocode is not actual code that can be run directly, and flowcharts are graphical.
They are both ways to describe algorithms, but they represent them differently.

quiz.stem: What does time complexity describe?
options: The number of steps an algorithm takes for one fixed input
How an algorithm’s running time changes as input size increases
The amount of input data stored on a computer
The time taken to write an algorithm
rationales: This is not the general description of time complexity because it does not consider changes in input size.
This is correct because time complexity describes how running time changes as input size increases.
This describes input storage, not how running time changes.
Writing time is not what time complexity measures.

quiz.stem: Which statement best describes space complexity?
options: The memory used by an algorithm relative to input size
The speed of an internet connection
The number of people using an algorithm
The length of an algorithm’s name
rationales: This is correct because space complexity concerns memory use relative to input size.
Internet speed is not the memory used by an algorithm.
The number of people using it is not a measure of its memory use.
The length of an algorithm’s name has no bearing on space complexity.

quiz.stem: Which of these is an example of Big O notation?
rationales: O(n) is an example of Big O notation, but it is not the only correct option.
O(log n) is an example of Big O notation, but it is not the only correct option.
O(n²) is an example of Big O notation, but it is not the only correct option.
This is correct because all three expressions are examples of Big O notation.

quiz.stem: What does space complexity help us evaluate?
options: To measure how much memory an algorithm uses
To draw a picture of an algorithm
To make an algorithm use no input
To count the number of people who use an algorithm
rationales: This is correct because space complexity concerns an algorithm’s memory use.
Drawing an algorithm is not what space complexity measures.
Algorithms may need input, and space complexity does not remove it.
Counting users does not measure the memory used by an algorithm.

quiz.stem: When considering time complexity, what should we examine?
options: Using a longer list always means fewer steps
The number of steps may change as the input size changes
Input size has no relation to an algorithm’s running time
All algorithms take the same time
rationales: A longer list does not always mean fewer steps.
This is correct because time complexity considers how running time changes with input size.
Input size is central to time complexity, so this statement is incorrect.
Different algorithms can take different amounts of time.

quiz.stem: What is a dry run of an algorithm?
options: Manually following an algorithm with sample data
Writing an algorithm in a programming language
Measuring the size of a computer’s memory
Removing all the steps from an algorithm
rationales: This is correct because a dry run involves checking an algorithm step by step with sample data.
Writing code is not the same as manually checking an algorithm.
Measuring the whole computer’s memory is not a dry run.
Removing steps would change the algorithm rather than test it.

quiz.stem: What does it mean to dry run an algorithm?
options: Run the algorithm on a computer and record its speed
Manually follow the algorithm using sample data
Change the algorithm without checking it
Draw only the input and output symbols
rationales: This describes measuring performance, not manually tracing the steps.
This is correct because a dry run manually follows the algorithm with sample data.
Changing an algorithm is not a dry run and may introduce errors.
A dry run follows the algorithm's steps rather than drawing only symbols.

quiz.stem: When dry running pseudocode, what should you do with variable values?
options: It records the value of each variable as the steps are followed
It converts a flowchart into a programming language
It removes all input from the algorithm
It guarantees that the algorithm is the fastest possible
rationales: This is correct because tracking variable values shows how the pseudocode changes its data.
Converting to code is not the same as manually simulating pseudocode.
A dry run uses sample input rather than removing the input.
A dry run can help check logic, but it does not prove the algorithm is fastest.

quiz.stem: In FindMax, num1 = 6 and num2 = 11. What happens when the condition num1 > num2 is checked?
options: The condition is True, so max = num1
The condition is False, so max = num2
The algorithm stops before assigning max
rationales: This is incorrect because 6 is not greater than 11.
This is correct because the condition is False, so the else branch assigns num2 to max.
The algorithm continues into the else branch and assigns max.
FindMax compares the values; it does not add them.

quiz.stem: A dry run of an addition flowchart uses A = 3 and B = 5. What value is displayed?
rationales: This is only the first input, not the sum.
This is correct because 3 + 5 = 8.
This is not the sum of the sample inputs.
This is not the sum; the flowchart adds 3 and 5.

quiz.stem: What is one purpose of dry running a flowchart?
options: To understand how a flowchart works step-by-step without using a computer
To make a flowchart execute itself
To replace every decision with an output
To make the algorithm use more input values
rationales: This is correct because manually tracing a flowchart helps you understand its control flow and find logic errors.
A dry run is a manual check; it does not make a flowchart execute itself.
A dry run follows the decisions rather than replacing them.
A dry run uses sample data to check the algorithm; it does not require more inputs.

quiz.stem: Which statement is NOT given as a benefit of simulation in this section?
options: Guaranteed to match every real-world event exactly
rationales: Cost-effective is listed as a benefit of simulation.
Safe is listed as a benefit because dangerous situations can be tested without risk.
Repeatable is listed as a benefit because a simulation can be run again with different settings.
The section lists cost, safety and repeatability, but does not promise that simulations exactly match every real-world event.

quiz.stem: What does LARP stand for?
options: Logic of Algorithms for Resolution of Problems
Language and Arithmetic for Repeated Programs
Lists of Algorithms for Real Programming
rationales: Correct: LARP stands for Logic of Algorithms for resolution of Problems.
Incorrect: This is not the expansion given for LARP.
Incorrect: This is not the expansion given for LARP.
Incorrect: This is not the expansion given for LARP.

quiz.stem: Which command begins a LARP algorithm?
rationales: Incorrect: READ is used to input values, not begin the algorithm.
Incorrect: WRITE displays messages or results; it does not begin the algorithm.
Correct: A LARP algorithm begins with START.
Incorrect: ENDIF closes a conditional structure, not the whole algorithm.

quiz.stem: What is the purpose of the LARP command WRITE?
options: To display a message or result
rationales: Correct: WRITE displays messages or results.
Incorrect: READ is used to input a value.
Incorrect: START begins the algorithm.
Incorrect: ENDIF finishes the IF structure.

quiz.stem: Which LARP command is used to input a value?
rationales: Incorrect: WRITE displays information.
Correct: READ inputs a value for the algorithm to use.
Incorrect: END finishes the algorithm.
Incorrect: IF begins a decision condition.

quiz.stem: Which standard flowchart symbol represents a decision?
rationales: Incorrect: A rectangle represents a process.
Correct: A diamond represents a decision.
Incorrect: A parallelogram represents input or output.
Incorrect: A circle is not the standard decision symbol described here.

quiz.stem: Which LARP structure is used to handle decision-making?
rationales: Incorrect: START and END mark the beginning and ending of the algorithm.
Incorrect: READ and WRITE handle input and output.
Correct: IF...THEN...ELSE is used for decision-making.
Incorrect: THEN and ENDIF are parts of the conditional structure, but the complete decision form is IF...THEN...ELSE.

quiz.stem: How does LARP help learners understand algorithms?
options: To make complex coding syntax harder
To see how algorithms process data by running them
To replace every flowchart with a picture
To prevent learners from testing different inputs
rationales: Incorrect: LARP uses a simplified approach rather than making syntax harder.
Correct: Running algorithms lets learners see how they process data and produce results.
Incorrect: LARP can execute algorithms, including those developed from flowcharts; it does not replace every flowchart with a picture.
Incorrect: LARP helps learners see the effects of different inputs.

quiz.stem: Which command ends a complete LARP algorithm?
rationales: Correct: END marks the end of a LARP algorithm.
Incorrect: ENDIF closes an IF conditional structure.
Incorrect: ELSE introduces the alternative branch of a conditional.
Incorrect: WRITE displays information and does not end the algorithm.

quiz.stem: An algorithm runs without stopping, but produces the wrong result because it uses an incorrect decision condition. What kind of error is this?
rationales: A syntax error is caused by something written incorrectly in the algorithm or flowchart.
A runtime error happens while the algorithm is executing, such as an attempt to divide by zero.
A logical error makes an algorithm behave incorrectly even though it can still run.
A missing comment may make an algorithm harder to understand but is not itself one of the three main error types described here.

quiz.stem: Which situation is an example of a runtime error?
options: The algorithm contains a spelling mistake in a step.
The algorithm tries to divide by zero while executing.
The algorithm gives a wrong answer because its logic is incorrect.
rationales: Writing a step incorrectly is an example of a syntax error.
Trying to divide by zero is an impossible operation that can cause an error during execution.
Incorrect logic that gives a wrong result is a logical error.
Comments help explain an algorithm, but having no comments is not the runtime-error example given in this section.

quiz.stem: Which technique involves going through an algorithm step by step to find where it goes wrong?
rationales: Tracing means following each step to identify where the problem occurs.
Removing all decision steps does not help locate the cause and may change what the algorithm is meant to do.
Changing every variable name is not a debugging technique described in this section.
Ignoring an error message can mean missing useful information about the problem.

quiz.stem: How can comments help with debugging?
options: Use comments to explain what each part should do.
Delete the algorithm and start a different problem.
rationales: Comments explain the intended purpose of parts of an algorithm, which can help reveal mistakes.
Deleting the algorithm does not explain or fix the error in the existing work.
Checking conditions is an important debugging technique, so avoiding it would not help.
Testing smaller parts separately is recommended, rather than using only larger problems.

quiz.stem: What does the LARP message “Undefined Variable” most likely mean?
options: A variable has been used before it is defined.
A condition gives the wrong result but the algorithm still runs.
A flowchart uses an incorrect symbol.
A comment does not describe a step.
rationales: The message means that a variable is being used without having been defined yet.
A wrong condition is a logical error, not the meaning of “Undefined Variable.”
An incorrect symbol may cause a syntax error, but it does not describe an undefined variable.
A comment that does not describe a step may be unclear, but that is not what this message means.

quiz.stem: Which LARP error message is associated with an operation that is not allowed, such as dividing by zero?
options: A comment written in the wrong place
rationales: “Missing Step” means an important step may have been left out.
“Undefined Variable” means a variable has not been defined before it is used.
“Invalid Operation” refers to an operation that is not allowed, such as dividing by zero.
The section does not identify a misplaced comment as the message for an operation that is not allowed.

quiz.stem: Which debugging technique is especially useful when a problem is difficult to check all at once?
options: Test the entire problem only after completing it.
Break the algorithm into smaller parts and test each part separately.
Remove all input values from the algorithm.
Use comments instead of checking the algorithm.
rationales: Testing only after completing the entire problem makes it harder to isolate the part causing an error.
Simplifying the problem means breaking it into smaller parts and testing each part separately.
Removing all input values does not help test whether the algorithm works with data.
Comments can help, but they do not replace testing and checking the algorithm.

quiz.stem: Which statement about syntax and logical errors agrees with this section?
options: Logical errors are always pointed out by LARP.
Syntax errors are usually easiest to find because LARP often points them out.
Runtime errors happen only before an algorithm is executed.
rationales: Logical errors can be hard to find because the algorithm may still run.
The section says syntax errors are easiest to find because LARP usually points them out.
Runtime errors happen while the algorithm or flowchart is being executed.
Comments can explain parts of an algorithm, but they do not automatically fix syntax errors.

quiz.stem: What does CSS stand for?
rationales: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.
Computer Style Sheets is not the expansion of CSS.
Creative Style Sheets is not the expansion of CSS.
Colorful Style Sheets is not the expansion of CSS.

quiz.stem: Which of the following tag is used to create a hyperlink in HTML?
rationales: `<link>` is generally used to link external resources, not to create a text hyperlink.
`<a>` creates a hyperlink, usually with an `href` attribute.
`<href>` is not an HTML element; `href` is an attribute commonly used on `<a>`.
`<nav>` identifies a section of navigation links but does not itself create a hyperlink.

quiz.stem: Which property is used to change the background color in CSS?
rationales: `color` sets the color of text and other foreground content, not the background color.
`background-color` directly sets an element’s background color.
`bgcolor` is an obsolete HTML attribute, not the CSS property for this purpose.
`background` is a CSS shorthand that can set a background color, but `background-color` is the direct property asked for.

quiz.stem: Which HTML attribute is used to define inline styles?
rationales: `class` assigns a class name and does not itself define inline styles.
`style` is the HTML attribute used to provide inline CSS declarations.
`font` is not the HTML attribute for defining inline styles.
`styles` is not the HTML attribute for defining inline styles.

quiz.stem: Which of the following is the correct syntax for a CSS rule?
rationales: A CSS rule uses a selector followed by braces containing property-value declarations separated by a colon.
This uses an equals sign instead of the required colon between a property and its value.
This uses an equals sign instead of the required colon and omits the terminating semicolon in the usual declaration syntax.
This incorrectly places a colon between the selector and its declaration block.

quiz.stem: How do you include JavaScript in an HTML document?
rationales: The `<script>` element with a `src` attribute is the standard way to include an external JavaScript file.
`<java>` is not the standard HTML element for including JavaScript.
`<js>` is not the standard HTML element for including JavaScript.
`<code>` does not load an external JavaScript file through a `src` attribute.

quiz.stem: Which HTML tag is used to create an unordered list?
rationales: `<ol>` creates an ordered list.
`<ul>` creates an unordered list.
`<li>` represents an individual list item rather than the list container.
`<list>` is not the standard HTML element for creating a list.

quiz.stem: Which tag is used to display a horizontal line in HTML?
rationales:
`
` inserts a line break rather than a horizontal line.
`<hr>` represents a thematic break and is commonly displayed as a horizontal line.
`<line>` is not the standard HTML element for displaying a horizontal line.
`<hline>` is not an HTML element.

quiz.stem: What is web development?
options: Creating and maintaining websites and web applications
Writing documents without using a computer
rationales: This is correct because web development involves creating and maintaining websites and web applications.
This is incorrect because repairing hardware is not the meaning of web development.
This is incorrect because writing ordinary documents is not web development.
This is incorrect because connecting to the internet alone does not create a website.

quiz.stem: Which technology is described as the skeleton or structure of a web page?
rationales: This is correct because HTML provides the structure of a web page.
This is incorrect because CSS is used to control the page's appearance.
This is incorrect because JavaScript is used to make a page interactive.
This is incorrect because a browser displays web pages but is not the page's structure.

quiz.stem: Which technology makes a web page look nice by controlling its style?
rationales: This is correct because CSS styles the appearance of a web page.
This is incorrect because HTML provides the page's structure.
This is incorrect because JavaScript adds interactive behaviour.
This is incorrect because a text editor is a tool for writing code, not a styling language.

quiz.stem: Which technology can make a web page interactive?
rationales: This is correct because JavaScript is used to make web pages interactive.
This is incorrect because HTML mainly provides structure.
This is incorrect because CSS mainly controls appearance.
This is incorrect because a web address identifies a location on the web but does not add interaction.

quiz.stem: Which benefit of learning web development helps a learner understand how websites are made and how the internet works?
rationales: This is correct because digital literacy includes learning how websites are made and understanding the internet.
This is incorrect because entrepreneurship is about starting an online business or service.
This is incorrect because creativity is about designing appealing and interactive websites.
This is incorrect because career opportunities concern possible jobs in the IT industry.

quiz.stem: Which benefit is practised when a developer works out why a website is slow and fixes it?
rationales: This is correct because finding and fixing a problem develops problem-solving skills.
This is incorrect because choosing a name does not describe the problem-solving benefit in the example.
This is incorrect because buying a computer is not the skill being practised.
This is incorrect because memorising web addresses does not explain how a developer fixes a website problem.

quiz.stem: Which activity best shows the creativity benefit of web development?
rationales: This is correct because a portfolio can use creative layouts, colours, and interactive features.
This is incorrect because repairing a printer is not an example of creating a website.
This is incorrect because writing a paper letter does not use web development.
This is incorrect because installing a fan is unrelated to designing a web page.

quiz.stem: Which example best illustrates entrepreneurship using web development?
options: Creating a website to sell handmade crafts
Learning how to fix a slow website
rationales: This is correct because creating a website to sell crafts is an example of starting an online business.
This is incorrect because fixing a slow website illustrates problem-solving.
This is incorrect because choosing colours illustrates styling and creativity, not starting a business.
This is incorrect because learning how websites are made illustrates digital literacy.

quiz.stem: Which task is mainly performed by HTML in front-end development?
rationales: Correct: HTML structures content such as headings, paragraphs, images, and links.
Incorrect: CSS styles content, including its colours, fonts, and layout.
Incorrect: JavaScript adds interactivity to web pages.
Incorrect: Databases store and manage data.

quiz.stem: Which technology is used to style the content on a web page?
rationales: Incorrect: PHP is a back-end programming language.
Correct: CSS styles web-page content, including colours, fonts, and layout.
Incorrect: HTML structures web-page content.
Incorrect: JavaScript adds interactivity to web pages.

quiz.stem: Which front-end technology can make a web page interactive?
rationales: Correct: JavaScript adds interactivity and can support features such as forms and animations.
Incorrect: A web server stores and delivers web pages to users.
Incorrect: A database stores and manages data.
Incorrect: HTML structures the content on web pages.

quiz.stem: What is a web server?
options: A computer that stores and delivers web pages
A language used only to style pages
A list of instructions stored in a database
rationales: Correct: A web server stores and delivers web pages when users enter a URL.
Incorrect: Styling web pages is the role of CSS, not a web server.
Incorrect: Creating images is not the definition of a web server.
Incorrect: A database manages data, while a web server delivers web pages.

quiz.stem: What is the main role of a database in back-end development?
options: It changes the layout of a page
It delivers a web page when a URL is entered
rationales: Correct: Databases store and manage information such as user details and website content.
Incorrect: CSS is used to change page layout.
Incorrect: A login button is part of the user interface, not the database's main role.
Incorrect: A web server delivers web pages to users.

quiz.stem: Which work is included in full-stack development?
rationales: Incorrect: Full-stack development is not limited to HTML and CSS.
